_comment: Core loop step 9: the Lodestar deck (docs/core_loop_plan_2026_10_01.md 4.1). One card per campaign, drawn from the campaign seed. first_hint and bearings are player-facing; director is for the story director. Bearing N becomes findable once gate class N+1 is open (Class II..VI); the fifth marks the system. Authored, original, and clear of the fixed-cast canon (checked by run_secret_leak_tests and run_lodestar_tests).

cards.title: The Lighthouse
cards.first_hint: A navigation beacon on repeat, sending course corrections for gates that aren't on any chart.
cards.nova_first: Hear that? Someone out past the deep gates is still giving directions to ships that stopped coming generations ago. That's either very sad or very useful.
cards.director: A beacon station older than the current gate charts. A salvage clan has kept it running for generations, trading its old network maps for supplies. It still knows routes nobody else remembers.

bearings.text: The beacon's corrections are for a gate network laid out before the present charts. Its maps are older than ours.
bearings.nova: Old maps that still work. I hate how much I want them.

bearings.text: Its signal is stronger past the Class III gates. Someone boosts it now and then: a person, not an automatic relay.
bearings.nova: Somebody is maintaining that thing. By hand. Out there.

bearings.text: Traders who reached it say a family runs it, and pays for spare parts in charts no registry has.
bearings.nova: A whole family living on a beacon. And selling the way out, one chart at a time.

bearings.text: The beacon's own course corrections point back at itself: follow them in reverse and they converge.
bearings.nova: It's telling every ship where to go, and where it is, in the same breath. Clever.

bearings.text: The corrections converge on one system past the edge of the charts. The Lighthouse is there.
bearings.nova: That's it. That's where it's been shouting from all this time.

cards.arrival: The clan's elder trades the old network map for news of the gates the Captain has crossed. The map shows the next horizon.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE LIGHTHOUSE
arrival_scene.approach: There it is. A beacon tower, still lit. Take us in close, Captain.
lines: Unregistered ship, you're the first to follow our corrections all the way in for a long time. Welcome to the Lighthouse.
My family has kept this light burning for six generations. We trade in news. Tell us which gates you've crossed, and we'll tell you where they go.
That's a fair trade. Here's a copy of our old network map. Most of it is roads nobody drives any more. Not all of it.
arrival_scene.nova: An old map that still works, from people who kept a light on for strangers. I think I like it out here.
arrival_scene.farewell: Before you go: there's something on the far edge of our map we never dared to chase. Maybe you will.

cards.title: The Silent Fleet
cards.first_hint: Ships reported missing out here are all last seen heading the same way, and none of them ever called for help.
cards.nova_first: Ships vanish all the time. They don't usually all vanish in the same direction, politely, without a single distress call.
cards.director: A colony convoy that chose to go dark: they jumped beyond the charts to escape a war, and switched off every transponder so nobody could follow. Their descendants still live there, and very much want to stay hidden.

bearings.text: An old registry lists forty ships that left together and never arrived anywhere. All of them were civilian.
bearings.nova: Forty ships of families, not soldiers. Nobody sends a fleet like that into nothing.

bearings.text: A deep-space buoy logged them passing in formation, with every transponder switched off by hand.
bearings.nova: They turned themselves off. On purpose. That's not an accident, that's a decision.

bearings.text: A freighter captain swears she saw lights on a world past the deep gates where no colony is registered.
bearings.nova: Lights where nobody lives. Either she was drunk, or somebody does.

bearings.text: Someone out there buys medicine and seed stock through brokers, always paying in very old coin.
bearings.nova: They're alive. And careful. And running low on things you can't grow.

bearings.text: The brokers' deliveries all go to one quiet system past the edge of the charts. The fleet is there.
bearings.nova: Found them. Let's be gentle about it. They went to a lot of trouble not to be found.

cards.arrival: The fleet's settlement, wary but polite. They ask the Captain to keep their secret, and offer something rare in return.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE SILENT FLEET
arrival_scene.approach: Ships. Dozens of them, all dark, all parked in neat rows. Slowly, Captain.
lines: Hold your position, stranger. You followed the brokers' trail. Not many people bother.
Our grandparents switched off their transponders to get away from a war. We'd like to stay switched off.
Keep this place off your charts and we'll call it even. Take this for the trouble: seed stock and ship parts, the old good kind.
arrival_scene.nova: Forty ships of families, and they're fine. They're actually fine. I'm keeping their secret, Captain. You should too.
arrival_scene.farewell: One more thing. Our scouts heard something further out. We didn't go and look. You look like the type who would.

cards.title: The Humming Gate
cards.first_hint: Gate techs whisper about a ring out past the deep gates that still works perfectly. Every other gate is falling apart.
cards.nova_first: A gate that works perfectly. You know how I feel about gates. I'd still like to see one that isn't trying to kill us.
cards.director: An intact gate from before the network's decline, still humming at full strength. Several factions want control of it, because whoever holds it can repair the others.

bearings.text: Gate techs say every ring was once tuned from one master gate, and that it was never found broken.
bearings.nova: One gate that set the tune for all the others. That explains why they're all out of tune now.

bearings.text: The deeper the gate, the more its fold drifts toward a single frequency: the hum.
bearings.nova: They're all leaning toward it. Like plants toward a window.

bearings.text: A repair crew went looking for the master gate and came back with perfect tuning data, then refused to say where from.
bearings.nova: Somebody's been there. And somebody paid them to forget.

bearings.text: Two factions are quietly buying gate parts in bulk, both shipping them the same way.
bearings.nova: Nobody buys that many gate parts unless they're planning to fix a lot of gates. Or own the one that can.

bearings.text: The hum is loudest at one system past the edge of the charts. The Humming Gate is there.
bearings.nova: That's the one. Listen to it. It sounds healthy. I didn't know they could.

cards.arrival: The ring itself, perfect and quiet, with two factions' ships already circling. Who gets it is the next season's question.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE HUMMING GATE
arrival_scene.approach: Listen to that. It's humming in tune. Every other ring I've ever heard sounds like a sick engine.
lines: This is a survey picket. You're in a restricted system. Then again, so are we, and we didn't ask either.
That ring hasn't missed a beat since before anyone kept records. Every gate tech alive would give a hand to study it.
Two factions are already circling. You got here first, so you get the readings. Use them before somebody decides they own the sky.
arrival_scene.nova: A perfect ring. I'm recording the hum, Captain. If the other gates ever need tuning, I know what they should sound like.
arrival_scene.farewell: The readings point somewhere. The ring was tuned by something further out, and it's still out there.

cards.title: The Cartographer's Chart
cards.first_hint: A dead surveyor's chart turned up at auction with one system circled, and its name scratched off the registry.
cards.nova_first: Someone scratched a whole system out of the registry. You can't lose a star by accident. Somebody wanted it gone.
cards.director: A famous surveyor found a system rich in rare ore and a navigable route beyond it, and a powerful consortium erased it from the registry to mine it in secret. The surveyor's notes survive in pieces.

bearings.text: The surveyor's last expedition filed every system but one. The missing entry was deleted by a registry clerk the same week.
bearings.nova: Deleted in a week. That's not bureaucracy, that's an order.

bearings.text: A page of the surveyor's notes describes ore readings no known belt matches.
bearings.nova: If those readings are real, that rock is worth more than this whole sector.

bearings.text: A consortium has been running unmarked haulers deep, and their manifests never list a destination.
bearings.nova: Unmarked haulers, blank manifests. Somebody found the surveyor's system first.

bearings.text: The scratched-out name survives in an old fuel log: the surveyor refuelled there twice.
bearings.nova: Twice. So it's real, and you can get back from it.

bearings.text: The fuel log's coordinates match one system past the edge of the charts. The circled system is there.
bearings.nova: There it is. Let's go and see what was worth erasing.

cards.arrival: The erased system: a consortium's secret mine, and the surveyor's route beyond it. The Captain decides who learns it exists.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE CIRCLED SYSTEM
arrival_scene.approach: The surveyor's station. Still standing, mostly. Let's see what they found.
lines: Automated survey log, recovered. Last entry: the belts here are richer than anything on the registry. And there's a route beyond them.
Second entry, different hand: consortium claim. System removed from the public registry. Mining under seal.
Third entry, the surveyor again: if you're reading this, the chart got out. Good. Finish the route for me.
arrival_scene.nova: They erased a whole system to keep it for themselves. And one stubborn surveyor said no. I wish we'd met them.
arrival_scene.farewell: The surveyor's last route runs on, past the edge of this chart. They never got to the end of it.

cards.title: The Garden
cards.first_hint: Ice haulers swear there's a green world past the dark, where nothing should be able to grow.
cards.nova_first: A green world out past the deep gates. Haulers say a lot of things after a long run. They don't usually all say the same thing.
cards.director: A living world around a dim star, warmed by a natural quirk of its orbit. A small group of botanists settled it long ago and has kept it off every map to protect it from mining.

bearings.text: Haulers deep out report seed pods frozen in the ice they cut: real ones, not from any known world.
bearings.nova: Seeds in the ice. They came from somewhere that grows things.

bearings.text: A botanist's paper, decades old, describes a world that should be frozen but keeps itself warm.
bearings.nova: A world that keeps itself warm. I'd like to know how. I'd like to know how for us.

bearings.text: Somebody out there trades fresh fruit for metal tools, and only through one hauler family.
bearings.nova: Fresh fruit. Out here. I don't even eat and I'm jealous.

bearings.text: Mining consortiums have been asking about the hauler family. Not kindly.
bearings.nova: And now the miners have noticed. Of course they have.

bearings.text: The hauler family's routes all end at one system past the edge of the charts. The Garden is there.
bearings.nova: Found it. Let's get there before the people with drills do.

cards.arrival: The Garden: a green world and its quiet keepers, and the mining fleet two jumps behind. What the Captain does next shapes the season.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE GARDEN
arrival_scene.approach: Captain. It's green. An actual green world, out here. I didn't believe the haulers.
lines: You found us. Please don't land, the ground is fragile. We can talk from orbit.
Our founders were botanists. A quirk of this world's orbit keeps it warm, and we've kept it off every map so it stays that way.
There's a mining fleet two jumps behind you, asking about the ice haulers' routes. Take these seeds. If anyone asks, you found nothing.
arrival_scene.nova: A garden, Captain. A whole living world. Let's not be the reason someone puts a drill in it.
arrival_scene.farewell: The keepers say the haulers' oldest routes go further still. Not everything out there is dead.

cards.title: The Quiet War
cards.first_hint: Salvagers trade rumours of a battlefield past the deep gates that nobody remembers fighting.
cards.nova_first: A whole battle nobody remembers. Wars are loud, Captain. Somebody had to work very hard to make one this quiet.
cards.director: Two factions fought a short, brutal war over a deep system and then agreed to erase it from their histories. The wrecks still guard what they fought over: a cache of pre-decline technology.

bearings.text: Salvagers sell hull plates from ships of two factions that, officially, have never fought.
bearings.nova: Two navies that never fought, and here are their pieces in the same crate.

bearings.text: Both factions' records skip the same eight months, as if nothing happened in that time.
bearings.nova: Same eight months missing on both sides. That's not a gap, that's a treaty.

bearings.text: A veteran in a deep station bar says the fight was over something neither side wanted the other to have.
bearings.nova: They'd rather nobody had it than the other side. That's how most bad things start.

bearings.text: The salvage gets newer, and better, the deeper it was found. The wrecks were guarding something.
bearings.nova: The closer to the middle, the better the ships. They put their best around whatever it was.

bearings.text: The wreck fields thicken around one system past the edge of the charts. The battlefield is there.
bearings.nova: That's the battlefield. Fly carefully. Some of those wrecks may still have opinions.

cards.arrival: The silent battlefield and what it guarded. Both factions' salvagers arrive within days, and they remember everything.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE QUIET WAR
arrival_scene.approach: Wrecks. Hundreds of them, still in formation. Nobody ever cleaned this up.
lines: Automated defence picket. Combat is over. Combat has been over for a very long time. Please state your faction.
Neither side? Acknowledged. The cache was never claimed. Both sides agreed to forget it existed.
Releasing salvage rights to the first neutral vessel. Message ends. Picket shutting down. Thank you for coming.
arrival_scene.nova: A whole war that both sides decided to forget, and a machine that waited all this time to hand over the keys. That's the saddest thing I've ever seen.
arrival_scene.farewell: The picket's last log points further out. Something there was worth starting a war over, too.

cards.title: The Hollow Market
cards.first_hint: A trader paid her docking fee in coin no station mints, and said she got it inside a comet.
cards.nova_first: Inside a comet. Either she's lying, or someone out there is running a shop in a snowball. I'd like to know which.
cards.director: An ungoverned bazaar bored into the core of a long-period comet that swings through the deep systems. No flag, no law, no records; debts and names can be bought clean there. Its keepers re-bore the openings every pass so no fleet can take it.

bearings.text: Goods with no registry stamp keep surfacing in the deep markets, all packed in the same ice-cut crates.
bearings.nova: Same crates, no stamps. One supplier, and they don't want to be found.

bearings.text: A debtor everyone thought ruined walked into a station with a clean name and new papers. He'd been 'out at the Market'.
bearings.nova: A new name, bought clean. That's either wonderful or terrifying.

bearings.text: Pilots past the Class III gates report a comet that answers hails with a price list.
bearings.nova: A comet with a price list. I've officially heard everything.

bearings.text: The comet's orbit is on old charts, but its openings are never in the same place twice: the keepers re-bore them every pass.
bearings.nova: They move the doors so nobody can lay siege. Clever. Paranoid, but clever.

bearings.text: The comet's next pass brings it through one system past the edge of the charts. The Hollow Market is there.
bearings.nova: Found it. Keep a hand on your wallet, Captain.

cards.arrival: A lawless bazaar inside a comet, where names and debts are bought and sold. The Captain is handed a route the haulers use when they don't want to be followed.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE HOLLOW MARKET
arrival_scene.approach: A comet with lights inside. Those are lanterns, Captain. People live in there.
lines: You've found the Market. No flags, no names, no questions.
Everything's for sale here: fuel, parts, a clean record, new papers. Just remember everything has a price, and we always collect.
You came the long way, so here's something free: a route the haulers use when they don't want to be followed. Don't say where you got it.
arrival_scene.nova: A whole economy nobody owns. I hate it. I want to see every shop.
arrival_scene.farewell: Before you go: the comet's next pass runs further out than any chart. Some of our best customers come from there.

cards.title: The Last Shipyard
cards.first_hint: A hauler swears she saw a ship being built in deep space so big it had docking lights before it had engines.
cards.nova_first: A ship bigger than a station, still unfinished, out past the gates. Someone's been building something for a very long time.
cards.director: A drydock where one family of shipwrights has spent four generations building a single enormous ship, the Long Promise, to their great-grandmother's plans. It has never flown. The family has argued for decades about whether it should, and who gets to say so.

bearings.text: Deep foundries keep filling orders for hull plate in one odd gauge nobody has built ships with in a century.
bearings.nova: Somebody's building to an old pattern. A very old, very big pattern.

bearings.text: An old engineer in a dockside bar carries her grandmother's plans for a ship 'longer than a gate is wide'.
bearings.nova: Longer than a gate is wide. So it can never leave. Unless it was never meant to.

bearings.text: Haulers who deliver to the far yards are paid in carved fittings and promises, never in credits.
bearings.nova: Paid in promises. Whoever runs that yard has more faith than money.

bearings.text: Welding light shows on the far lanes every shift, every year: someone has never stopped working.
bearings.nova: Four generations of welders. That's not a job, that's a family vow.

bearings.text: The plate orders all ship to one system past the edge of the charts. The Last Shipyard is there.
bearings.nova: There it is. Let's go and see a ship nobody's finished.

cards.arrival: A family drydock four generations into building one great ship. The shipwrights trade their charts for the Captain's honest word on where it could ever go.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE LAST SHIPYARD
arrival_scene.approach: Look at the size of that hull, Captain. And it's still in scaffolding.
lines: Mind the sparks, stranger. You're looking at the Long Promise. My great-grandmother laid her keel, and we've been building her ever since.
Half the family says she's ready to fly. The other half says she was never meant to. We vote every year, and nobody wins.
You've seen the lanes out there. Tell us honestly: is there anywhere left worth flying her to? Take our charts in trade for your answer.
arrival_scene.nova: Four generations, one ship, and they still can't agree what it's for. I love these people.
arrival_scene.farewell: If you find somewhere worth sailing to, come back and tell us. We'll finish her faster.

cards.title: The Archive
cards.first_hint: A court on the frontier threw out a deed as forged, and the owner produced a certified copy no court had ever seen. 'From the Archive,' he said.
cards.nova_first: A copy nobody knew existed, of a paper everybody swore was fake. Somebody out there keeps everything.
cards.director: An order of record-keepers on a station drifting in a gas giant's upper clouds. For generations they have copied every registry, deed and court ruling filed in the region, including the ones that were destroyed. They take no sides and sell nothing: a copy costs only an honest answer to why you need it.

bearings.text: Court clerks in three systems describe the same visitor: a quiet copyist who asks for nothing but a look at the ledgers.
bearings.nova: Someone's reading every court ledger in the region. Politely.

bearings.text: A family won back land they'd lost forty years ago, on the strength of a ruling everyone believed was burned.
bearings.nova: Burned papers that turn up anyway. I'm starting to like these people.

bearings.text: Haulers past the Class III gates carry sealed crates of blank ledger film one way, and never bring anything back.
bearings.nova: Blank film in, nothing out. Whatever they write, it stays there.

bearings.text: Gas-giant skimmers talk about lights in the high clouds that never drift with the wind.
bearings.nova: Something floating in a gas giant on purpose. That's a lot of trouble for privacy.

bearings.text: The film shipments all end at one giant past the edge of the charts. The Archive is in its clouds.
bearings.nova: There it is. Let's go and see who's been keeping score.

cards.arrival: A record-keepers' station in a gas giant's clouds, holding every deed and verdict ever filed, burned ones included. The Captain is given their index of the old routes.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE ARCHIVE
arrival_scene.approach: Lights in the clouds. Those are reading lamps, Captain. Hundreds of them.
lines: Welcome to the Archive. We keep the record. All of it, including the parts people paid to have forgotten.
We don't sell copies and we don't take sides. We only ask why you need a page, and we write your answer down too.
You've come a long way with nothing to ask for. That's rare. Take our index of the old routes; it's the least-read thing we hold.
arrival_scene.nova: Every deed, every verdict, every lie anyone tried to burn, all in one place. I could read here for a hundred years.
arrival_scene.farewell: The oldest page we hold mentions a place beyond the charts. We've never had a visitor from there. You could be the first.

cards.title: The Neutral Ground
cards.first_hint: Two factions at each other's throats both sent envoys out past the gates, unarmed, on the same day.
cards.nova_first: Enemies, unarmed, on the same day, going the same way. There's only one kind of place where that happens.
cards.director: The decommissioned treaty station where old enemies signed the peace that ended the last war. Each side built its own half, in its own style; the halves meet at one central hall. It is still the only place the factions meet unarmed. Its keepers, descended from both delegations, enforce one rule: no weapon past the hall door.

bearings.text: Old war records mention a peace signed 'at the halfway hall', but no station by that name is on any chart.
bearings.nova: A peace signed somewhere nobody can find. Very careful, or very convenient.

bearings.text: Envoys from rival factions refuel at the same deep depot, a day apart, and never speak.
bearings.nova: Two delegations, same road, same silence. They're going to the same table.

bearings.text: A gunsmith grumbles that every envoy's ship comes back to her to have its weapons refitted.
bearings.nova: Everyone disarms to go there. Interesting kind of place.

bearings.text: Traders describe a station built in two styles that don't match, joined in the middle by one hall.
bearings.nova: Two halves that don't match. Somebody built that from both ends and met in the middle.

bearings.text: The envoys' fuel stops all point to one system past the edge of the charts. The Neutral Ground is there.
bearings.nova: Found it. Holster everything, Captain. I mean it.

cards.arrival: The treaty station where enemies still meet unarmed. Its keepers hand the Captain their list of who has been talking to whom.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE NEUTRAL GROUND
arrival_scene.approach: Two stations joined at the hip. One half's all angles, the other's all curves. That's the treaty hall in the middle.
lines: Weapons cold before the hall door. That's the only rule here, and it has held for sixty years.
My grandmother sat on one side of that table and my grandfather on the other. They signed the peace, then married. Somebody has to keep the hall.
The factions still send envoys here when talking is cheaper than fighting. Take our list of who's been talking to whom. Out there it's worth more than guns.
arrival_scene.nova: Sixty years of enemies at one table, held together by one rule. That's braver than any war.
arrival_scene.farewell: Before you go: the treaty names a third delegation that never arrived. Their road ran past the charts. Maybe you'll find out why.

cards.title: The Halo
cards.first_hint: A bounty hunter came back empty-handed and furious: her mark had 'rung the bell', and couldn't be touched.
cards.nova_first: A bell that makes you untouchable. Either it's a very good story or a very strange law.
cards.director: A loose circle of small candle-lit pilgrim chapels on tethers round a central bell-buoy, in a system whose red star is dying. By an old covenant every faction still honours, anyone who rings the bell is under sanctuary: no one may be taken from the Halo against their will. Its keepers are a quiet order who tend the candles and keep the name of everyone who has ever rung.

bearings.text: Debt collectors keep a private list of names marked 'rang the bell', and never chase them again.
bearings.nova: A list of people even collectors give up on. I want to know what's on the other end of that.

bearings.text: Pilgrims buy candles by the crate at the deep stations, and won't say what they're for.
bearings.nova: Crates of candles, going somewhere dark. Romantic, or a fire hazard.

bearings.text: A fugitive turned herself in, then walked free when the court learned she'd spent a year at the Halo.
bearings.nova: Even the courts respect it. That's a lot of power for a bell.

bearings.text: Navigators past the Class III gates mark one dying red star 'do not hunt here' in the margins of their charts.
bearings.nova: Do not hunt here. Hand-written. I like these navigators.

bearings.text: The margin notes all point to one red star past the edge of the charts. The Halo circles it.
bearings.nova: There it is. Let's go and hear that bell.

cards.arrival: A sanctuary of candle-lit chapels where no one may be taken away. The keepers give the Captain their pilgrims' charts of the quiet roads.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE HALO
arrival_scene.approach: Candles. Hundreds of little lights on tethers, round that red star. It's a ring of chapels, Captain.
lines: Peace, traveller. You've come to the Halo. Whoever rings the bell here can't be taken away against their will. That's the whole of our law.
Debtors, runaways, the sorry and the hunted have all rung it. We don't ask what they did. We only keep their names, so they're never forgotten.
You haven't come to ring it, so you've come to see. Take our pilgrims' charts; they know the quiet roads.
arrival_scene.nova: A whole sanctuary built on one promise, and everyone still keeps it. I didn't think the frontier had anything this gentle.
arrival_scene.farewell: The keepers say the first bell came from somewhere beyond the charts. Nobody here remembers where. Maybe you'll find it.

cards.title: The Wellhead
cards.first_hint: Every water contract in the frontier is stamped with the same small seal: a drop over a crack.
cards.nova_first: Everyone's water, signed in one place. Whoever holds that seal could make the whole frontier thirsty.
cards.director: A small ice moonlet whose vent geyser waters the whole frontier. One family runs the rig towers over the vent, and every water contract in the region is signed at its table. Not villains: they've kept the price fair for a century. They're tired, and the vent is slowing, and nobody outside knows.

bearings.text: Water haulers out past the gates all fill at the same depot, and all carry the same seal on their manifests.
bearings.nova: One seal on every water manifest. That's not a market, that's a tap.

bearings.text: Old miners say the price of water hasn't changed in a hundred years, no matter how dry the year.
bearings.nova: A fair price for a century. Somebody out there is either a saint or very careful.

bearings.text: Ice dust drifts down the deep lanes in a slow stream that always comes from the same direction.
bearings.nova: Ice drifting downstream from one place. Follow the water.

bearings.text: A hauler swears the depot's tanks were half empty, for the first time in living memory.
bearings.nova: Half empty. For the first time. And nobody's said a word about it.

bearings.text: The ice stream leads to one moonlet past the edge of the charts. The Wellhead is there.
bearings.nova: There it is. The tap the whole frontier drinks from.

cards.arrival: The ice moonlet that waters the frontier, and the tired family that runs it. They trust the Captain with their secret and their survey of the deep ice fields.

arrival_scene.speaker: THE WELLHEAD
arrival_scene.approach: A little ice moon with a plume coming off it, and towers all over it, Captain. That's the Wellhead.
lines: Welcome to the Wellhead. Every drink of water on the frontier starts here, under our feet.
My family has signed every water contract for a hundred years and never raised the price. Not once. People forget that.
Here's something nobody else knows: the vent is slowing. Take our survey of the deep ice fields; someone will have to find the next well.
arrival_scene.nova: The whole frontier's water rests on one tired family. I didn't expect to feel sorry for them.
arrival_scene.farewell: If the next well is out there, it's past the charts. Find it before the frontier finds out we're running dry.
